prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: I can’t name a single objectively “best” lawyer — the best choice depends on your case facts and which lawyer’s experience, communication style and track record fit you. I can, however, help you find a small list of excellent Dallas truck‑accident lawyers and tell you exactly how to choose among them.

How to pick a top truck‑accident lawyer
- Relevant experience: look for attorneys who focus on trucking/serious personal injury and who routinely handle commercial‑vehicle cases (not just general PI).
- Trucking‑specific knowledge: experience with FMCSA rules, cargo/shipper liability, lease/owner‑operator relationships, black box (ECM) data and accident reconstruction.
- Trial and settlement record: ask about recent verdicts and multi‑million dollar settlements in truck cases.
- Resources: the firm should have investigators, accident reconstruction experts and medical/legal resources to handle complex truck claims.
- Reputation & peer review: Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, Martindale‑Hubbell, and peer nominations are useful signals.
- Client reviews & references: read client testimonials and ask the attorney for recent client references.
- Communication & accessibility: confirm how often you’ll get updates and who handles day‑to‑day contact.
- Fee structure: most truck cases are handled on contingency (commonly 33–40% plus costs). Get the fee agreement in writing.
- Discipline check: verify the lawyer’s standing and any disciplinary history on the State Bar of Texas website.

Practical questions to ask at a free consultation
- How many truck cases have you handled in Dallas/Fort Worth?
- How many went to trial vs. settled? Example outcomes?
- Do you handle ECM/electronic data recovery and hire accident reconstructionists?
- Who will be my point of contact?
- Do you advance case costs? What are the contingency fee and costs policy?
- What is your timeline estimate and what would you need from me?

Important legal timelines
- Texas generally has a 2‑year statute of limitations for personal injury (Texas Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code § 16.003). Don’t delay in contacting an attorney.

Where to find vetted Dallas truck‑accident lawyers
- State Bar of Texas “Find a Lawyer”
- Dallas Bar Association lawyer referral
- Texas Trial Lawyers Association member directory
- Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, Martindale‑Hubbell, Avvo

If you want, I can:
- Put together a short list (3–5) of Dallas truck‑accident lawyers with high ratings and trucking experience (I’ll include contact info, notable verdicts/settlements, fee info and how many years’ experience). Tell me your zip code or neighborhood and whether you prefer a big firm or a boutique trial firm.
- Or draft an email/list of questions you can use when you call for consultations.

Which would you prefer?
